MONKEYBUSINESS Customer Guide Welcome to Monkeybusiness Organisations rely on information spread across documents, customer records, operational systems, and data used to build or assess AI. Teams often spend time moving that information between tools, checking formats, resolving exceptions, and confirming who approved a change. Monkeybusiness is a proposed B2B software platform for coordinating those tasks. Its focus is workflow automation for AI-training operations and practical enterprise data management: moving approved inputs through defined steps and making status, quality checks, and review points easier to follow. Who this guide is for This guide is for business and operations leaders, data and machine-learning teams, IT and risk reviewers, project owners, and potential implementation partners. It introduces the proposed service, gives examples of possible workflows, and outlines questions to resolve before any real deployment. What to expect The following pages cover the concept’s capabilities, sample use cases, implementation approach, responsible data practices, support model, and contact directory. Feature availability, integrations, pricing, security controls, and service commitments would need to be established before a real product launch. A practical principle Automation should make routine work more dependable without hiding how it happened. People need understandable status, a way to investigate exceptions, and authority to review decisions that matter.2

MONKEYBUSINESS Customer Guide Our story, mission, and direction The idea Preparing information for business use or AI development can involve collecting approved sources, cleaning records, applying labels, checking quality, tracking changes, and managing access. When every team builds a separate process from spreadsheets and disconnected tools, work can become difficult to repeat or audit. Monkeybusiness is a proposed response to that challenge: bring common data tasks into clearer workflows that teams can configure, review, and improve. This is a positioning statement, not a record of company history. Mission and vision Our proposed mission is to make enterprise data and AI-training operations more accessible, efficient, and accountable through thoughtful automation. We envision teams preparing and managing useful data without reinventing a manual process for every project. Operating principles • Clarity: show workflow status, actions, and exceptions in plain language. •Human accountability: keep review and approval at important decision points. •Customer control: make permissions and process responsibilities explicit. •Measured improvement: compare outcomes with an agreed baseline. •Pragmatism: prioritise useful workflows over automation for its own sake.

MONKEYBUSINESS Customer Guide Services and platform capabilities The capabilities below describe the proposed offering; they are not a guarantee that a particular feature or integration is currently available. AI-training workflow automation Coordinate approved dataset inputs through cleaning, classification or annotation, validation, human review, approval, versioning, and export preparation. Teams can define routing rules and quality checks for routine work while directing ambiguous records to a reviewer. Enterprise data management Organise information with structured intake, field mapping, metadata, ownership, and data-quality checks. Role-based access and workflow histories can help teams understand who may use information and how it changed, when those controls are supported and configured. Integrations and orchestration Connect defined steps across supported storage, business systems, and review queues. Each integration should have an agreed scope covering authentication, data mapping, error handling, and system ownership. Operational visibility Give teams a view of work in progress, items awaiting review, failed checks, and recurring exceptions. Reports should distinguish measured results from estimates and make it possible to investigate an issue. Scope boundary: workflow automation can support data operations, but it does not independently guarantee model accuracy, data quality, legal compliance, or business results. Those depend on the source material, implementation, customer decisions, and use case.

MONKEYBUSINESS Customer Guide Illustrative customer use cases These examples show where a workflow platform might help. They are not descriptions of completed deployments or customer results. Preparing a dataset A team brings together authorised records, checks required fields and formats, identifies duplicates or missing values, and routes uncertain cases to trained reviewers. Review outcomes and dataset versions are recorded before an approved export. The model team still assesses whether the data suits its intended purpose. Managing enterprise knowledge An organisation registers approved policies and process documents, assigns owners, standardises metadata, and flags stale or conflicting material. If search or AI retrieval is added, access should respect source permissions and responses should be evaluated. Recurring business operations Finance, sales, support, or product teams may repeatedly receive files, validate formats, reconcile fields, request missing information, and publish reports. A defined workflow can standardise routine steps and notify a person when a rule fails. Choosing a starting point A promising pilot has a clear trigger and end state, repeatable steps, an accountable owner, accessible and authorised data, and a measurable baseline such as processing time or error rate. Define what may run automatically and how a person can pause, review, or reverse an action.

MONKEYBUSINESS Customer Guide Getting started: implementation A successful rollout begins with one bounded workflow and a shared definition of success. The steps below are a proposed approach that can be adapted to an actual product and customer.1. Discover: identify the problem, people involved, current systems, bottlenecks, data types, and desired outputs.2. Scope a pilot: name an owner, define what is included and excluded, agree on approvals, and record a baseline.3. Prepare data and access: confirm permission to use the data, retention needs, sensitivity, source of truth, and access roles. Start with a test environment or representative sample when possible.4. Configure and test: map fields, define rules, connect supported tools, and test normal cases plus missing data, unexpected formats, duplicates, and service failures.

5. Launch carefully: release to a limited group, monitor completion and exceptions, and make sure users know how to report issues or request review.6. Review: compare results with the baseline and adjust, maintain, or expand the workflow based on evidence. Before launch • A business owner and technical contact are assigned. •Data permissions, success measures, and acceptance criteria are documented. •Exception handling and human approval paths are defined. •Test cases include failure conditions, and users know where to get help. Do not send credentials or sensitive records through ordinary email. Use only approved data and channels.6

MONKEYBUSINESS Customer Guide Data protection and responsible AI This section is a customer diligence checklist, not a statement that Monkeybusiness holds any certification or automatically complies with every law. Resolve these questions with the actual provider before production use. Questions for review • What information is collected, stored, logged, exported, or shared with subprocessors? •Where is data hosted, and how are users authenticated and permissions managed? •What encryption, retention, deletion, backup, and recovery controls are provided? •Are administrative actions and workflow changes logged?How are incidents reported? •Is customer data used to train or improve a model?What export and service-exit options apply?Responsible data operations Automation can apply process rules; it cannot by itself establish that data is lawful, fair, representative, or suitable. Customers should confirm source rights, consent or licensing requirements, sensitive-data handling, annotation guidance, quality thresholds, and escalation routes.

If AI-generated labels or classifications are used, check them against an appropriate human-reviewed sample and track known limitations. Apply stronger review and documentation when the intended use carries greater impact. Shared responsibility The provider should document the controls and commitments it actually supplies. Customers remain responsible for having authority to submit data, configuring access, reviewing outputs, and meeting their own legal and organisational duties. Contracts and data-processing terms should define the exact responsibilities. Before sharing sensitive data: review the current contract, privacy and security documentation, data-processing terms, and available configuration options. The sample contacts in this guide are not security-reporting channels.7

Plan an evaluation For an initial conversation, outline the workflow, teams involved, systems used, approximate volume, data sensitivity, and the result you want to measure. Do not send confidential data in an initial enquiry. Useful questions include: • What workflow is in scope, and what is explicitly excluded? •Which systems and formats are supported today? •How do exceptions, review, approvals, and data deletion work? •What are the implementation, usage, subscription, and support costs? •

How will success be measured, and how can data be exported if needs change?Closing Monkeybusiness is a concept for making business information more usable and recurring data work more dependable. The proposed focus is practical automation with visible checks, human review, and clear customer responsibilities. A real evaluation should begin with a specific workflow, agreed safeguards, and an outcome both teams can measure. Make your data work harder.monkeybusiness.example 10
